components.name: Status bar
components.description: Status bar showing native OS-rendered icons (signal, wifi, battery, time). The design system represents these as-is for documentation only and does not control their styling.

properties.name: Theme
properties.notes: Controls icon and text colour — must match the surface behind the status bar

properties.name: System
properties.notes: Switches between iOS and Android icon sets and layout conventions

variants.name: Transparent
variants.semantic_use: Over images, gradients, or dark hero surfaces — uses onwhite icon assets

variants.name: Light
variants.semantic_use: Over light/white surfaces — uses onblack icon assets

variants.name: Dark
variants.semantic_use: Over dark solid surfaces — uses onwhite icon assets

variants.name: iOS
variants.semantic_use: iPhone / iOS — uses *-IOS onblack.svg (Light) or *-IOS onwhite.svg (Transparent / Dark)

variants.name: android
variants.semantic_use: Android devices — uses *-Android onblack.svg (Light) or *-Android onwhite.svg (Transparent / Dark)

rules: Never place Status bar directly on a screen. Always use the Top bar organism — the Status bar is already embedded inside it.
The design system does not style or override status bar icons — use only the listed assets.
Always match the icon set to the surface theme — the wrong set on a dark or light background produces invisible or illegible icons.
Never replace status bar icons with custom artwork.
Time text in the status bar is always OS-rendered — never mock it with a static text layer in production.
Use viewBox on all SVG assets to ensure correct proportional scaling across device sizes.

components.name: App bar
components.description: Sits at the very top of the screen content area (below the OS status bar). Provides the primary identity and top-level navigation context for the current app surface.

properties.name: Type
properties.notes: Controls left-side treatment

properties.name: R-slot
properties.notes: Reveals a right-side slot for custom components (e.g. search, CTA)

properties.name: R-icon
properties.notes: Reveals a right-side icon action (e.g. notification bell, settings)

properties.name: Count (L-icon)
properties.notes: Nested Icon button property — number of icons shown in the left slot; icons stack horizontally. Icon size locked at 24px.

properties.name: Count (R-icon)
properties.notes: Nested Icon button property — number of icons shown in the right slot; icons stack horizontally. Icon size locked at 24px.

variants.name: Default
variants.semantic_use: Standard app bar with logo/wordmark on the left
variants.example: All standard screens — home, listing, detail pages

variants.name: Profile
variants.semantic_use: Left side shows a profile avatar instead of a logo
variants.example: Screens where the signed-in user's identity is the primary context (e.g. account home, personal feed)

use_cases.context: Right side needs a non-icon component (search bar, notification badge with avatar, CTA button)
Right side icon-only actions (settings gear, filter, notification bell, share)
use_cases.config: R-icon=True, set Count to add up to 4 icons

rules: The App bar is always full-width and pinned to the top of the content area — never scrolls with content.
Do not use the App bar inside a bottom sheet or modal — use Title bar instead.
Only one App bar per screen.
Do not add additional navigation items to the App bar — use Tab - Stack or Section header for in-page navigation.
Icon size in both L and R icon slots is always 24px — never override this.
Use Count on the nested Icon button to control how many icons appear; do not stack separate icon instances manually.

components.name: Title bar
components.description: Provides a screen or section title, optional body text, and optional flanking icons/slots. Used inside modals, bottom sheets, sub-pages, and anywhere a full App bar is not appropriate. Single component with no variant axis.

properties.name: Title text
properties.notes: The primary screen/section label

properties.name: Body text
properties.notes: Supporting subtitle or description

properties.name: Body
properties.notes: Toggles the body/subtitle text line

properties.name: L-slot
properties.notes: Left slot — typically a back button or close icon

properties.name: L-icon - Title
properties.notes: Icon left of the title text

properties.name: R-icon - Title
properties.notes: Icon right of the title text

properties.name: R-icon - Body
properties.notes: Icon right of the body text

properties.name: L-icon - Body
properties.notes: Icon left of the body text

properties.name: R-slot
properties.notes: Right slot — for a CTA button, avatar, or action component

properties.name: R-overflow
properties.notes: Gradient overflow fade on the right edge — used when title text is long

use_cases.config: L-slot=False, R-slot=False (handle drag area takes the place of navigation)
L-slot=True (back arrow), optional R-slot for action
L-slot=True (close icon), Title text set to modal name
Body=True with Body text set to context info

rules: Never place Title bar directly on any screen, layout, modal, or bottom sheet. Always use the Top bar organism — the Title bar is already embedded inside it.
Do not use Title bar as a section header inside a page or list — use Section header instead.
Do not use Title bar to add a heading or title to a bottom sheet or modal — those surfaces have their own header patterns; place Top bar only at the top of a full screen.
Do not use Title bar as an in-page title or content heading — it is a navigation component, not a typographic element.
Always set Title text — never leave the default 'Title' placeholder in production.
Set Body=True only when a subtitle genuinely adds context; do not use it for decorative purposes.
R-overflow=True is for design articulation only — ensure truncation is handled in code via text-overflow: ellipsis.
L-slot and R-slot accept any component — use Icon (atom) or Button (molecule) only.

components.name: Section row item
components.description: Individual rows used inside a section or list containing a left label, an optional right label, and a separator. Represents an actionable or informational pairing between two pieces of data (label and value, category and count, setting name and state).

properties.name: Size
properties.notes: Controls row height and text size

properties.name: Style
properties.notes: Controls visual weight of the row

properties.name: Separator
properties.notes: Shows/hides the dot (·) separator between the L label and R label

properties.name: R Label
properties.notes: Toggles the right-side label

properties.name: L - Label
properties.notes: Left-side label — the key / category

properties.name: R - Label
properties.notes: Right-side label — the value / action

variants.name: Small
variants.semantic_use: Dense data rows, compact settings lists

variants.name: Medium
variants.semantic_use: Default — standard list rows, settings

variants.name: Large
variants.semantic_use: Prominent actionable rows, touch-target-critical contexts

variants.name: Primary
variants.semantic_use: Full visual weight — stronger text and border treatment; default rows, primary content areas

variants.name: Tertiary
variants.semantic_use: Lighter visual weight — subdued text and border; secondary info rows, supplementary content

use_cases.config: L - Label='Notifications', R - Label='On', Style=Primary, Separator=True
L - Label='Amount', R - Label='₹1,200', Style=Primary, R Label=True
L - Label='Electronics', R - Label='24', R Label=True for count

use_cases.context: Rows where labels need no separator
use_cases.config: Separator=False — hide the dot when the two labels read as a single continuous value

rules: Use Separator=False when the dot between the two labels would be visually confusing or redundant — e.g. when the L and R labels together form a single continuous value.
Use R Label=False only when the row is purely label-only and no value or action is needed.
L - Label and R - Label are content properties — always populate them with real content; never leave 'Label' as the final text.
Do not use Section row item as a full-page navigation row — use List (organism) for navigation patterns.
Section row items are stacked vertically — never placed side by side.

components.name: Nudge
components.description: A floating action bar fixed at the bottom of the screen. Its vertical position depends on the content below it (bottom nav, CTA, etc.) and is set by the designer per screen. Communicates status, warnings, errors, success states, or contextual guidance without a modal or toast.

properties.name: Variant
properties.notes: Sets the semantic colour and icon treatment

properties.name: L - icon
properties.notes: Leading icon on the left (typically a semantic icon matching the variant)

properties.name: R - icon
properties.notes: Trailing icon on the right (typically a dismiss/close icon)

properties.name: Link text
properties.notes: Shows an inline text link/CTA at the end of the label

properties.name: Label text
properties.notes: The nudge message content

variants.name: Default
variants.semantic_use: Neutral info / general guidance
variants.example: Add UPI ID to enable faster payments

variants.name: Success
variants.semantic_use: Positive confirmation

variants.name: Error
variants.semantic_use: Validation failure / error state
variants.example: UPI ID not found. Please check and retry.

variants.name: Warning
variants.semantic_use: Caution / non-blocking alert
variants.example: Your session will expire in 2 minutes

use_cases.context: Successful action confirmation below a button
Informational tip in a settings section
Expiry warning on a limited-time offer

rules: Nudge is a bottom-floating bar — never placed inline within content flow. Its vertical offset above other bottom elements is defined by the designer per screen.
Always set Label text to the actual message — never leave the default placeholder.
Use L-icon=True as the default — the semantic icon reinforces the variant meaning. Only turn it off when space is critically constrained.
Link text=True is for a single actionable link only — do not use it as a general CTA button; use a Button atom for primary actions.
R-icon is typically a dismiss/close affordance — only use it when the nudge can be manually dismissed.
A screen should contain at most one Nudge at a time per content zone.

components.name: Inline action row
components.description: A horizontal container that holds a row of inline action items — typically icon-label pairs, quick-action chips, or compact navigation items. Used inside cards, sections, and panels where a compact row of actions is needed.

properties.name: L + R padding
properties.notes: Adds left and right padding when true — use when the row lives inside a padded container

properties.name: Divider
properties.notes: Shows/hides the top or bottom divider line separating the action row from adjacent content

variants.name: L + R padding=false
variants.semantic_use: Row is edge-to-edge (e.g. inside a full-bleed card or a section with no outer padding)

variants.name: L + R padding=true
variants.semantic_use: Row has its own horizontal breathing room (e.g. inside a padded card or list section)

use_cases.context: Quick action row at the bottom of a card
Action row inside a padded settings section
Last action row in a panel (no trailing separator)

rules: The Inline action row is a layout container — populate its internal slots with the correct action atoms (Icon, Button, or Chip).
Set Divider=False on the last row in a section — a trailing divider is incorrect.
Use L + R padding=true only when the row's parent container does not already provide horizontal padding — do not double-pad.
Do not use the Inline action row as a primary navigation element — it is for compact supplementary actions only.

components.name: Seaction header
components.description: Labels a content group and optionally provides a body/subtitle line, flanking icons, a right slot, and an overflow treatment. Placed directly above a list or grid of related items. (Component name typo 'Seaction header' is intentional — matches Figma.) Single component with no variant axis.

properties.name: Title text
properties.notes: The section label / group name

properties.name: Body text
properties.notes: Optional supporting subtitle or description

properties.name: Body
properties.notes: Toggles the body/subtitle text line

properties.name: L-icon - Title
properties.notes: Icon left of the title

properties.name: R-icon - Title
properties.notes: Icon right of the title (e.g. info icon, status indicator)

properties.name: L-icon - Body
properties.notes: Icon left of the body text

properties.name: R-icon - Body
properties.notes: Icon right of the body text

properties.name: R-slot
properties.notes: Right-side slot — for a 'See all' CTA, count badge, or icon button

properties.name: R-overflow
properties.notes: Gradient fade on the right edge of the title — for long or scrolling labels

use_cases.config: Title text set, all booleans off
R-slot=True, place a text Button or Link inside the slot

use_cases.context: Section with a count or badge
use_cases.config: R-slot=True, place a Badge inside the slot

rules: Always set Title text — never leave 'Title' as the production label.
Use Body=True only when a subtitle genuinely helps the user — not as decoration.
R-slot accepts any component — prefer Button (text variant), Badge, or Icon.
R-overflow=True is for design articulation only — handle truncation in code.
Section headers are not interactive themselves — any action belongs in the R-slot.
Do not use Section header to replace Title bar inside modals or sheets.

components.name: Chip
components.description: Compact interactive control used for filtering, selection, and categorical navigation. Comes as an individual unit.

properties.name: State
properties.notes: Controls the chip's interaction type

properties.name: Is active
properties.notes: Selected/active state

properties.name: Is disabled
properties.notes: Disabled state

properties.name: L-Icon
properties.notes: Leading icon inside the chip

variants.name: Toggle
variants.semantic_use: Simple on/off selection — no trailing indicator; filter chips, category selection

variants.name: Cross
variants.semantic_use: Active state shows a dismiss (✕) icon to deselect; applied filters that can be removed inline

variants.name: Dropdown
variants.semantic_use: Trailing chevron — opens a picker or menu; multi-value filters, sort options

variants.name: Switch
variants.semantic_use: Trailing toggle — binary on/off within the chip; feature toggles presented as chips

variants.name: Large
variants.semantic_use: Default — filter bars, category rows

variants.name: Med
variants.semantic_use: Dense layouts, nested filter areas

rules: Always use Chip - Stack for groups of chips — never place individual Chip atoms side-by-side manually.
Use Cross state for applied / removable filters — not for general selection.
Use Dropdown only when tapping the chip opens a picker — not as a decorative indicator.

components.name: Chip - Stack
components.description: A horizontal stack/row of chips with optional overflow fades and dividers between chips.

properties.name: Count
properties.notes: Number of chips in the row. Plenty renders a scrollable overflow state — use when the chip count is dynamic or unknown at design time.

properties.name: Size
properties.notes: Matches the individual Chip size

properties.name: L-overflow
properties.notes: Left edge fade — indicates chips are scrollable to the left

properties.name: R-overflow
properties.notes: Right edge fade — indicates chips are scrollable to the right

properties.name: Divider
properties.notes: Vertical divider between chips in the stack

rules: Always use Chip - Stack for groups of chips — never place individual Chip atoms side-by-side manually.
Use L-overflow and R-overflow together when a chip row is horizontally scrollable.
Divider=False should only be used when a visually clean separation-free row is required (rare).

components.name: .Tab Unit
components.description: Base tab unit. Used inside a custom layout or inside Tab - Stack. Not used standalone in final screens.

properties.name: Is active
properties.notes: Active/selected state

properties.name: Is disabled
properties.notes: Disabled state

properties.name: R-icon - Title
properties.notes: Icon to the right of the tab label

properties.name: L-icon - Title
properties.notes: Icon to the left of the tab label

properties.name: Title text
properties.notes: Tab label — set the text per tab context

rules: Always use a Stack component for final screens — never place individual Tab Unit atoms manually in a row.
The active tab must always be visually distinguishable — never set all tabs to Is active=False.

components.name: Tab - Stack
components.description: A horizontal row of standard underline tabs. Default tab pattern for in-page navigation.

properties.name: Count
properties.notes: Number of tabs. Plenty renders a scrollable overflow state — use when tab count is dynamic.

properties.name: R-overflow
properties.notes: Right edge fade — scrollable tabs overflow indicator

properties.name: L-overflow
properties.notes: Left edge fade — scrollable tabs overflow indicator

properties.name: Switch tab - Page swipe
properties.notes: Indicates the tab is linked to a horizontal page swipe — active tab follows swipe gesture

rules: Always use a Stack component for final screens — never place individual Tab Unit atoms manually in a row.
Use Plenty with overflow indicators (L-overflow, R-overflow) when tabs scroll horizontally.
Switch tab - Page swipe=True must be wired to a horizontal scroll/swipe container in code — not purely decorative.

components.name: Tab - Pill - Units
components.description: A single pill-style tab unit — used inside Tab - Pill - Stack.

components.name: Tab - Pill - Stack
components.description: A compact pill-style tab group — typically 2–3 options. Common for binary or ternary views (e.g. 'Monthly / Yearly', 'All / Income / Expense').

properties.name: Count
properties.notes: Number of pill tabs

properties.name: BG
properties.notes: Background fill on the pill container

properties.name: Selected
properties.notes: Which tab is currently selected

properties.name: Is disabled
properties.notes: Disabled state for the whole group

rules: Tab - Pill - Stack supports maximum 3 tabs — for more options use Tab - Stack.
The active tab must always be visually distinguishable — never set all tabs to Selected=False.

components.name: Tab - Fancy - Unit
components.description: An atom — a building block only. Never placed directly on a screen. Always use Image Tab w bg which composes these units into a ready-to-use tab bar.

properties.name: Selected
properties.notes: True = tab is in the active/selected state; False = tab is inactive

variants.name: True
variants.semantic_use: The tab is in the active/selected state

variants.name: False
variants.semantic_use: The tab is inactive

rules: Never use Tab - Fancy - Unit directly — always use Image Tab w bg, which composes these units into a complete tab bar.

components.name: Tab - Visual
components.description: Tabs that include an image, icon, or rich visual indicator alongside the label. An atom — a building block only. Never placed directly on a screen. Always use Tab - Visual - Stack instead.

properties.name: Type
properties.notes: W Image = tab with an image thumbnail; W Icon = tab with an icon; W Tab = tab with a nested sub-tab indicator

variants.name: W Image
variants.semantic_use: Tab with an image thumbnail

variants.name: W Icon
variants.semantic_use: Tab with an icon

variants.name: W Tab
variants.semantic_use: Tab with a nested sub-tab indicator

rules: Never use Tab - Visual directly — always use Tab - Visual - Stack instead.

components.name: Tab - Visual - Stack
components.description: A stack of visual tabs (image/icon/sub-tab) for media/category browsing with visuals.
rules: Never use Tab - Visual directly — always use Tab - Visual - Stack instead.

components.name: Bottom nav 2
components.description: The primary bottom navigational bar of the app. Fixed at the bottom of the screen, provides top-level destination switching across the three core app sections. Carries a Cart FAB that surfaces conditionally when the user is on the Shop tab with pending cart items.

properties.name: Tab
properties.notes: Sets which tab destination is currently active

properties.name: Collapsed
properties.notes: Collapses the nav bar — used when the screen needs full vertical space (e.g. scrolled state)

variants.name: Home
variants.semantic_use: Home feed / dashboard — user is on the home screen

variants.name: Shop
variants.semantic_use: Shop / marketplace — user is browsing the shop

variants.name: Card
variants.semantic_use: Card / payments — user is on the card or payments screen

variants.name: Collapsed=False
variants.semantic_use: Full nav bar visible — default for all standard screens

variants.name: Collapsed=True
variants.semantic_use: Nav bar collapses — use when scrolling or full-bleed content requires reclaiming vertical space; defined by designer per screen

rules: Bottom nav 2 is always fixed to the bottom of the screen — never scroll it with content.
Only one instance of Bottom nav 2 per screen.
Always set Tab to the active destination — never leave all tabs in an inactive state.
Collapsed=True is set by the designer per screen based on scroll behaviour — do not default to collapsed.
Cart FAB is only shown on the Shop tab when the user has pending cart items — do not show it on Home, Card, or any empty-cart state.
The Avatar (Brand type, 28px) next to the Cart FAB shows product images of the pending cart items — it is not a user profile avatar.

Chevron visibility on the Cart FAB is a product decision — the designer specifies the condition under which it appears (e.g. expandable cart drawer, proceed to checkout). Do not apply it without a defined interaction.
Do not detach or manually modify the embedded Cart FAB or Avatar sub-components — configure them through the exposed properties only.
Embedded sub-components: Cart FAB (floating cart action), Avatar (Brand type, 28px), Chevron (inside Cart FAB), Icon Wrapper (tab icon, size 20px).

rules: Error + Is Active and Success + Is Active (focused but empty) are not valid states — error and success only appear after a user has entered a value. A focused empty field is always Default + Is Active.
Always set Title text — never leave 'Title' as the production label.
Always set Placeholder text to contextual hint copy — never leave 'Placeholder'.
Use State=Error + Error text for validation failures.
Pre-filled and Post-filled are for non-editable prefix/suffix content (e.g. ₹, +91, .00) — not for default-filled values.
BG=False is for inputs on surfaces that already have a container background — prevents double-layering.

rules: Use Card - Stack for all lists of multiple cards — never manually stack individual Card instances.
Always populate Title text and Body text with real content — never leave 'Title' or 'Body' as production text.
Slot=0 is for header-only cards (e.g. a simple label card with no content rows).
Enclosed=False with BG=False is a ghost card — use only when the card must be visually frameless (e.g. inside a tinted surface that provides its own container).
Divider - Header=True separates the header from the first content slot — always use when both Header=True and Slot ≥ 1.
Only change nested divider Type or Colour if the card surface requires a different treatment — for most cards the defaults are correct.

components.name: ODP card
components.description: Offer Detail Panel card — a structured card used to display an offer, product, or detail entry with a header and an optional rating/info footer. Structure: .Header item (top bar), PDP Card slot (content), and .Footer item (only when Footer=True).

properties.name: Footer
properties.notes: Shows/hides the footer bar below the card

properties.name: Slot
properties.notes: Content slot inside the card body — preferred instance is OLP-list (any component)

use_cases.context: Product detail entry in a list

rules: Always populate L - Label and R - Label in .Header item with real content — these are the primary identifiers for the card.
Use Footer=True only when there is actual rating or supplementary data to display — do not use the footer as decoration.
The PDP Card slot is a free slot — place the appropriate product/offer component from the design library.
The Rating bar item inside the footer is display-only — do not wire an interaction to it directly; use a parent tap target wrapping the card.
Border radius: top-only radius when Footer=True — the footer attaches flush below the card body with bottom radius on the footer strip.
